# The Shift-Left Thesis {#sec-shift-left}

::: {.callout-note title="Executive summary" appearance="simple"}
- *(Phase C)*
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Drafter guidance" appearance="minimal"}
Target ~4,500 words. See `research/00-book-outline.md` Chapter 6. Open with the Databricks 16% number — the cleanest evidence available that the thesis holds at scale.
:::

## What "shift left" means in document pipelines

- The thesis: move **structural and semantic understanding** earlier in the pipeline — into parsing rather than after parsing.
- The opposite (and prior) approach: minimal parsing, heavy downstream cleanup. Plain OCR + regex + template + reconciliation logic.
- The shift-left approach: rich parsing that emits **structured, grounded, validated** output ready for direct downstream use.

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "Where the work moves under the shift-left thesis"
flowchart LR
    subgraph Classic
      A1[OCR] --> A2[Layout heuristics] --> A3[Template extraction] --> A4[Cleanup] --> A5[Downstream app]
    end
    subgraph Agentic
      B1[Agentic OCR<br/>extract + validate + ground] --> B2[Downstream app]
    end
```

## The economic argument

- Per-document **compute cost** goes up. Per-page rates for agentic parsing run 5–50× higher than commodity OCR.
- Engineering effort + downstream error-handling cost goes down faster.
- **Net cost-per-correct-output drops, not cost-per-page.** This is the headline.
- Databricks evidence: **16% performance gain across every agent framework** when `ai_parse_document` was inserted upstream — no reasoning-layer changes. The 16% is the cleanest available number.
- Databricks cost claim: **5–7× lower cost than comparable VLM-only pipelines** for the same downstream accuracy.

## Where complexity actually moves (not disappears)

- Complexity moves from downstream Python scripts into **eval infrastructure** (Chapter 11), **observability** (Chapter 15), and **HITL workflows** (Chapter 9).
- Anyone who claims agentic OCR eliminates pipeline work has not deployed it. Pipeline work is reduced and relocated, not eliminated.
- The hidden cost: building golden sets, regression-testing prompts, monitoring drift, managing vendor version pinning. None of these existed in the classic IDP world.

## Honest counter-arguments

- **Cost-per-page does rise.** For commodity high-volume invoice processing at scale, classic IDP can still win on TCO. The shift-left thesis is not universal.
- **Latency increases.** Multi-pass reflection adds wall-clock time. Real-time use cases may need single-pass models.
- **Vendor lock-in increases.** Agentic OCR vendors are stickier than classic OCR. Switching costs are higher.
- **The 16% gain has caveats.** It's measured on Databricks' own OfficeQA benchmark, which is new and Databricks-published. Treat as directional, not authoritative.

## A worked ROI example

- 100,000 pages/month healthcare prior-auth workflow.
- Baseline: classic IDP at $0.04/page = $4,000/month parsing + 25% HITL = $X downstream cost.
- Agentic: Reducto or Landing AI at $0.015/page = $1,500/month parsing + 5% HITL = $Y downstream cost.
- Net: agentic is ~3× more expensive on parsing, but downstream costs drop enough that **net per-correct-extraction is lower**.
- Caveat: numbers vary wildly by vertical. Generic invoice processing at 1M+ pages/month tips back toward classic IDP.

## Shift-left is not about model size

- A small, layout-aware model **shifts left harder** than a large model called naively.
- PP-StructureV3 at <100M params matches Gemini-2.5-Pro on OmniDocBench — and PP-StructureV3 is doing shift-left in a way the large model isn't.
- Granite-Docling-258M is the strongest 2026 example of "small model, shifted left."

## Named takes

> *"Shift-left is a thesis about where structural understanding lives. It is not a thesis about model size. PP-StructureV3 at 100M params is shifting left harder than a 70B model called twice."*

> *"If you can articulate your ROI only in cost-per-page, you have not understood the shift-left thesis. The right denominator is cost-per-correct-extraction-with-provenance."*
